clue.text: Still road heads west to US port

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west means the piece is written right to left

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway, so MI is a crossword stand-in for a road
Mobile is a port city in Alabama

explanation.surface: A traffic report: the road is at a standstill as drivers head west for an American harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something still is motionless, unable or not trying to move.

clue.text: Friendly state

definitions.meaning: close and familiar, on very warm terms
to declare or make known, a verb

explanation.definitionFit: Intimate is both an adjective meaning close and a verb meaning to hint or announce.

clue.text: Keen to hear cock-crow

indicators.note: to hear means the word is listened to rather than seen

parts.note: cock-crow is dawn, the morning

explanation.surface: Eager to catch the rooster calling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like eager but means to wail in grief; MORN said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To keen is to wail in lament for the dead, so it means to grieve.

clue.text: Knocks over first drink with enjoyment

indicators.note: first says the drink is put before the other piece

parts.note: beer is a drink
with and and both mean together with
to skittle is to knock down, as in the game of skittles

explanation.surface: Someone toppling things after having a drink with relish.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is an idiom for pure fun, usually in 'life is not all beer and skittles'. Skittles is a British pub game like bowling.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means pleasure and amusement, an easy life.

clue.text: Willowy position in which sphagnum crops up crops up

indicators.note: the moss goes inside the position

parts.note: sphagnum is a kind of moss

explanation.definitionFit: Willowy and lissome both describe a slender, supple and graceful figure.

clue.text: Deplorable foul we perpetrated

indicators.note: something perpetrated is committed or carried out, so the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A complaint about some shameful foul play that we committed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perpetrated' rearranges FOULWE.
explanation.definitionFit: A deplorable effort is lamentable or pitiful, a synonym.

clue.text: Cox having had too much to drink?

definitions.meaning: the cox steers a rowing eight, the ninth person in the boat

definitions.text: having had too much to drink?
definitions.meaning: a British idiom for being a little drunk

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally describes the extra crew member of an eight and idiomatically means tipsy.

clue.text: Fancy-free John engaged in flirtation after I left

indicators.note: engaged in means placed inside, so one piece sits within the other
the word for flirtation is used once its I has departed

parts.note: playing footsie is flirting with the feet under a table
john and loo are both slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: A carefree man called John caught up in a flirtation after the speaker walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after I left' leaves FOOTSE; playing footsie is touching feet flirtatiously under a table, and 'engaged in' places the toilet slang inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Footloose means free to go where one likes, without ties, like fancy-free.

clue.text: Good in fast, hard distance

indicators.note: the first letter is placed inside the period of fasting

H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A good runner covering ground at a fast, hard pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts G inside LENT; 'fast' looks like speed but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A length is a measured distance from end to end.

clue.text: Tin that is discovered in river valley

parts.note: a tin is a can
yon is an old word for that, as in yon hill

explanation.surface: A tin can found lying in a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A canyon is a deep gorge, typically cut by a river.

clue.text: Grey-brown ribbon round Ursula's head

indicators.note: the ribbon is wrapped around the other piece, so it goes outside

parts.note: a ribbon is a strip of tape

indicators.note: the head of a name is its opening letter

explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts U (the head of Ursula) inside TAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Taupe is the name of a brownish-grey colour, from the French for mole.

clue.text: Snake who'd got involved in extortion

explanation.surface: A slippery character who got caught up in a blackmail racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got involved' rearranges SNAKEWHOD; the apostrophe is no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A shakedown is slang, chiefly American, for extortion of money by threats.

clue.text: Manual initially produced with a blue binding

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows

parts.note: with and and both mean together with

explanation.surface: An instruction book printed in a blue cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'binding' poses as a book's cover beside 'Manual', but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A binding rule is compulsory, one that must be obeyed.

clue.text: Capital abandoned by army man

indicators.note: the capital is left without the army, so those letters are removed

parts.note: Valetta, an older spelling of Valletta, is the capital of Malta
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A city deserted by its soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue relies on the older single-L spelling of the Maltese capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentleman's man is his manservant, a personal attendant who looks after his clothes.

clue.text: Lever altered but replaced

indicators.note: letters that are replaced are put back in different places, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A machine lever that was modified and then swapped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' rearranges ALTERED; 'but' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a foot-operated lever that drives a machine such as a sewing machine or loom.

clue.text: Mysterious giant mice have evolved

indicators.note: things that have evolved have changed form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzle: huge rodents have developed over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have evolved' rearranges GIANTMICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Enigmatic means puzzling and hard to interpret, a synonym.

clue.text: Fine point applied to shaft

parts.note: N, north, is a point of the compass
an arrow is a shaft fired from a bow

explanation.surface: A sharp tip being fitted to an arrow shaft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like praise but means slender.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine line or margin is a slim one, so fine is a synonym of slender.

clue.text: Ingredient of perfume revealing regional minute, variation

indicators.note: a slight variation means the letters are altered in their order

explanation.walkthrough: 'minute, variation' rearranges REGIONAL; 'revealing' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Geraniol is a rose-scented alcohol found in geranium oil and used in perfumes.

clue.text: In at this gate

parts.note: a batsman who is 'in' in cricket is batting at the stumps, and the same word is also a small gate

explanation.surface: Directions telling a visitor to come in through this gate.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batting player is said to be 'in'; the stumps they defend share their name with a small side gate.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the cricket stumps a batsman defends and a small door or gate.

clue.text: Part of insect god cut short

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder

indicators.note: short means the word is cut back by its last letter

parts.note: to axe is to cut

explanation.surface: A deity whose name has been trimmed to form an insect body part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' takes E off AXE to give AX.
explanation.definitionFit: The thorax is the middle body section of an insect, between head and abdomen.

clue.text: In bath, let everyone see fine physical specimen

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across these words

explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals letters lying within 'bath, let everyone'.

clue.text: Sport of changing soap's conclusion?

parts.note: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap opera

clue.text: A number of musicians, about 19 being superfluous in Perth

indicators.note: the Scots word goes about, or around, the other piece

parts.note: orra is a Scots word meaning odd or superfluous; Perth is a Scottish city

clue.text: At home, confined to bed, upset by medicinal preparation

clue.text: I work in a gallery, to arouse interest

clue.text: Time to position a tree

clue.text: Fail to amuse when speaking of occult rites
